say: Four ninety B.C. Ten thousand Athenians stand on the plain of Marathon.
Facing them: an army of the largest empire the world had ever seen.
Their general, Miltiades, did the unthinkable. He thinned his own center, and stacked both wings.
Then he ordered the charge. At a run. Nearly a mile, straight at the Persian line. The Persians thought they were insane.
The Persian center broke through. Right into the trap. And the wings swung shut.
Herodotus counts sixty-four hundred Persian dead. Athens lost one hundred ninety-two.
And that famous run to Athens? The run that really mattered was a hundred and fifty miles. Part two.
